result.summary:
Re-verified the prior diagnosis (WF03-ISS0692-20260916 step-01-issue-fixer) against the current tree: lib/letflow/design/req362-visual-regression-testing.md is confirmed present on main (this branch's base) with exactly the content the diagnosis quoted -- §1.3 ('Distinctness from transient screenshots', durable git-committed baselines, zero data-sensitivity caveat), §2.2/§4.1 with no content precondition, §7's AC map, and §8's four open questions (OQ-1..OQ-4), none of which already covered this gap. Spot-checked test/fixtures/uat/scenarios/swiftroute/tenant-onboarding-happy.yaml directly: actor 'Alice Bauer' / 'alice.bauer@swiftroute.example' / hostname 'swiftroute.bpm.example' confirmed disclosed-fictional per the file's own header-comment provenance ('Ported verbatim from R-Co... disclosed-synthetic fixtures'). Confirmed test/fixtures/uat/visual-baselines/ still does not exist anywhere in the tree -- no authenticated gui_screen scenario has yet produced a real baseline through this mechanism, so the diagnosis's premise (design-only fix, no retroactive baseline to fix) still holds.

DESIGN CHANGE APPLIED to lib/letflow/design/req362-visual-regression-testing.md:

1. New §1.5 'Data-sensitivity policy for baseline content (binding, not an open question)', inserted after §1.4 and before §2. States as a binding invariant: any gui_screen expected outcome accepted (§2) or re-baselined (§4) must be captured against synthetic/disclosed-fictional actor and tenant data only, never real tenant PII. Grounds this in the swiftroute scenario spot-check (not a new practice) and in §1.3's own permanence point (git-committed, superseded versions retained forever in history -- the property that turns an already-synthetic-by-convention screen into a standing risk the moment a future scenario deviates). States the rejection reasoning for the two alternatives ISS-0692's fix direction offered: redaction rejected because a pixel mask must be bit-for-bit stable forever against §3.4's unconditional mechanical diff or it becomes a second source of spurious failures; accepted-risk rejected because real PII in a permanently git-history-retained artifact is exactly the exposure class this project's security invariants exist to prevent. Notes explicitly this is an authoring-discipline invariant, not something acceptBaseline/rebaseline can mechanically verify from PNG bytes -- and states plainly it is deliberately NOT deferred to §8 as an open question.

2. §2.2 (accept action): added a 'Precondition (§1.5)' paragraph before its numbered steps, cross-referencing the new section.

3. §4.1 (re-baseline action): added a 'Precondition (§1.5)' paragraph, explicit that a re-baseline does not get a pass on this invariant merely because the baseline it replaces was already accepted.

4. §7's AC map: added a new row '(data-handling scope implicit in AC-1/AC-2 -- what may be captured into a permanent baseline) | §1.5 (binding synthetic/disclosed-fictional-data-only policy, cross-referenced from §2.2 and §4.1)'.

5. §8 left untouched -- no new open question added; the policy is a stated decision per the task's explicit instruction.

OPTIONAL DOCSTRING (my discretion, per the diagnosis's part (c) and the dispatch's explicit 'your call'): added a one-line-plus cross-reference to §1.5 in the JSDoc comments above both acceptBaseline and rebaseline in web/tests/support/visual-baseline.ts, stating the caller-side precondition and that it is not enforceable from PNG bytes. Judged worth adding: near-zero cost, makes the invariant visible at the call site for whoever implements the first real authenticated gui_screen scenario, and is explicitly comment-only -- does not add, or gesture at adding, any redaction/synthetic-data-enforcement code, so it does not trigger ISS-0692's AC2 implementation clause. No other change made to that file; acceptBaseline/rebaseline's logic, signatures, and error-throwing behavior are byte-for-byte unchanged.

No implementation/enforcement code was written anywhere (no redaction transform, no synthetic-data validator) -- consistent with (b)/(c) of the diagnosis and this dispatch's explicit instruction. AC2's implementation clause ('if a redaction or synthetic-data mechanism is chosen, it is implemented') is not triggered: the chosen policy is a content/authoring discipline, not a mechanism acceptBaseline/rebaseline's code enforces, and no baseline has yet been committed for the policy to apply retroactively to.
